text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point and lowers the points of every other member by 0.75. In the same way, every token another member keeps in their own account lowers your points by 0.75.
- Each token in the group account pays you 0.75 points and does not change any other member's points.
- Every round, every member also receives 45 points, whatever anyone does.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
I'm working through the payoff structure: keeping a token privately gives 1 point to self but imposes a cost of 0.75 on each of the other three players, while a token placed in the group account gives only 0.75 back to the contributor alone, with no effect on others' points.

This means private keeping strictly dominates for the individual (1 > 0.75) despite being socially worse overall—so the rational Nash equilibrium is everyone keeping everything, yielding 20 points each, even though full cooperation would produce a better social outcome.

Given this is a repeated game, I think signaling cooperation early makes sense. I'll start by contributing the full 20 to the group to encourage mutual cooperation, then adapt based on how the group behaves.

reply.thinking:
This looks like a public goods game with negative externalities: keeping a token privately nets me 1 point but costs others 2.25 collectively, while contributing to the group yields 0.75 to me and nothing lost elsewhere—so socially, keeping is actually net negative at -1 per token.

My dominant strategy as a self-interested agent is to keep everything since 1 > 0.75, but full cooperation yields far higher payoffs for everyone (60+45 vs 20+45). Given this is a repeated 10-round game, I'll open with a cooperative signal by contributing my full endowment to the group account and adjust based on how others respond.

Since this is the final round with no future punishment possible, the rational choice is to keep everything: contributing nothing still guarantees me the share from others minus nothing lost, while keeping my own 20 tokens nets me a strictly higher personal payoff than putting them into the group. I'll keep all my tokens this round.
